{{Short description|Hungarian philosopher, logician and physicist}}
{{primary sources|date=February 2024}}
'''Miklós Rédei''' (born October 4, 1952, in [[Budapest]], [[Hungary]])<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lccn.loc.gov/n97115815|title=Library of Congress LCCN Permalink n97115815|access-date=2024-03-19}}</ref> is a Hungarian [[Philosophy|philosopher]] who specializes in the [[philosophy of physics]].<ref name="personal">{{cite web|url=https://personal.lse.ac.uk/redeim/CV.pdf|date=2017-04-01|title=Curriculum Vitae {{pipe}} Miklós Rédei |access-date=2024-02-17}}</ref> He is professor of philosophy at the Department of Philosophy, Logic and Scientific Method at the [[London School of Economics]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Science |first=London School of Economics and Political |title=Miklós Rédei |url=https://www.lse.ac.uk/cpnss/people/miklos-redei.aspx |access-date=2024-02-17 |website=London School of Economics and Political Science |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Rédei holds an MA in physics and MA in philosophy from [[Eötvös Loránd University]], and a PhD in philosophy from the same university from 1982. He was awarded his doctorate ([[Candidate of Sciences]]) in physics in 1989, his [[habilitation]] in philosophy in 1997, and became [[Doctor of Sciences]] in philosophy in 2001.<ref name="personal"/> He has been an assistant professor at [[Eötvös Loránd University]], [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholar]] at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], [[University of California, Irvine]], senior fellow at the [[Dibner Institute for the History of Science and Technology]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and visiting fellow at the Munich Centre for Mathematical Philosophy at [[LMU Munich]].<ref name="mcmp.philosophie.uni-muenchen.de">{{Cite web |title=Redei, Miklos - Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy (MCMP) - LMU Munich |url=https://www.mcmp.philosophie.uni-muenchen.de/people/external_members/redei_miklos/index.html |access-date=2024-02-17 |website=www.mcmp.philosophie.uni-muenchen.de |language=en}}</ref>

Rédei has published extensively on the logical foundations of [[quantum mechanics]], [[probabilistic causation]], [[mathematical physics]], the [[history of mathematics]], as well as the life and works of [[John von Neumann]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=JSTOR: Search Results |url=https://www.jstor.org/action/doBasicSearch?Query=%22Mikl%C3%B3s+R%C3%A9dei%22&acc=on&wc=on |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=www.jstor.org}}</ref> 

== Books ==
Rédei is the author or coauthor of:
* ''Quantum Logic in Algebraic Approach'' (Kluwer, 1998).<ref>Reviews of ''Quantum Logic in Algebraic Approach'':
*Stanley P. Gudder (1998), ''Foundations of Physics'', {{doi|10.1023/A:1018801911508}}, {{MR|1611718}}
*Mirko Navara, {{Zbl|0910.03038}}
*Karl Svozil (2001), ''Studies in History and Philosophy of Science Part B'', {{bibcode|2001SHPMP..32..113S}}, {{doi|10.1016/S1355-2198(00)00005-8}}
</ref>
* ''The Principle of the Common Cause'' (with Gábor Hofer-Szabó and László E. Szabó, Cambridge University Press, 2013).

His [[edited volume]]s include:
*''John von Neumann and the Foundations of Physics'' (edited with Michael Stölzner, Kluwer, 2001)<ref>Reviews of ''John von Neumann and the Foundations of Physics'':
*Michael Dickson (2003), ''Philosophy of Science'', {{doi|10.1086/378876}}, {{jstor|10.1086/378876}}
*Tracy Lupher (2003), ''Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics'', {{bibcode|2003SHPMP..34..684L}}, {{doi|10.1016/S1355-2198(03)00070-4}}
</ref>
* ''John von Neumann: Selected Letters'' (American Mathematical Society, 2005).<ref>Reviews of ''John von Neumann: Selected Letters'':
*George Dyson (2007), ''Notices of the American Mathematical Society'', [https://www.ams.org//journals/notices/200706/tx070600724p.pdf]
*Christopher Lance (2008), ''Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society'', {{doi|10.1112/blms/bdn095}}
*Roman Murawski, {{Zbl|1092.01018}}
</ref>
*''The Vienna Circle in Hungary'' (edited with András Máté and Friedrich Stadler, Springer, 2011)<ref>Review of ''The Vienna Circle in Hungary'':
Maté Szabó (2013), ''The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic'', {{jstor|41825311}}
</ref>
